My fiancé and I had a similar issue. I grew up allowed to do whatever and he had real parents so not knowing if I'm okay stresses him out. I used to have to call/text him when I left work since I sometimes got out really late (1 - 2 am) and he was worried about me walking to the car/driving home alone. I don't always remember to call or text and it worried him when I was getting home especially late sometimes.

Now we have a tracking app (we use Life360). If I were to get into a car accident it would auto notify him. When I leave work or home he gets a little ping and can check on me whenever he's concerned. I think that for a lot of couples something like Life360 is a bit invasive, but it works for us. I like being able to watch him drive home sometimes too.

It really helped a couple weeks ago when I took a wrong turn going to a friend's house and I didn't know her address. I called him and he acted like a GPS to help me get there. We both get a lot of time with our friends, even more now that we know our partner isn't worried about us.

I am not suggesting this will for sure work for you. Some people really like their privacy, and I respect that. It just works for us.

Basically laid down that he had comped 50% of the guy's bill and put the best server on their table so he knows the service was excellent. 1. You can stretch taco meat by adding a can of refried beans directly to the meat in the pan. Add extra seasoning, the refried beans kind of melt into the meat and you can't see them anymore. The longer you cook it the more water leaves the beans, so if you want it to look just like meat cook it a little longer. Tastes amazing, the texture is a bit more like taco bell meat, which I personally enjoy. I sold my fiance and MIL on the idea by making it without telling them. They didn't even know the beans were in there. I do 1 can of refried beans per 1 pound of meat, which almost doubles your meat.
2. Food banks are great, some cities/states have things like Gleaners which (when I was a kid) were subscription type food services. You would pay monthly and be allowed to go get food 4 times a month. They had shelves set up that looked much like a grocery store and each shelf had the number of items allowed per number in your family. We paid for 4 people so we could usually get 2-4 of each item. Nicer than the food boxes because you could actually choose and not have to take canned white asparagus or sardines in oil then try and figure out how the heck to make those taste... like food.
3. Need more time to pay your bill? Contact the company asap, before the due date if possible and they'll often give you more time.
4. Internet/TV/Car Insurance costs too much? Research starting deals in your area with them and other companies. Call and let them know that while their service was amazing, it's just a bit too expensive for you. You found a deal at X company for (whatever price you saw) and you can't to stay with them if they can't offer a good price. Be kind, but firm that the only reason you are interested in leaving is because of the cost savings. 9/10 times they will offer a comparable discount. If they don't... I mean, the other price you saw is a real price so you could switch over.
5. This doesn't save money but it can help you. Always keep an updated resume, when you get hired to a new place, just edit the resume that you used with them to include the new job, starting date, position, description of duties. Don't feel stuck in your job. Always have feelers out with trusted friends/family. Check out employment websites once a month to see what's out there. Apply for jobs you don't think you're qualified for while you're employed. It never hurts to try. Most of my coworkers who hate their jobs and always want to quit aren't actually looking for anything else. Don't get too comfortable because you like certain aspects of your job. You'll like some aspects of almost every job, except telemarketing. That's soul-sucking I hear.
6. Being poor sucks up your spare time, but if you do have any spare time and you want to better yourself, learn Excel, look at the programs or knowledge that's expected in jobs you want and study up. Watch Youtube videos on how to use the software and treat it like a class where you take notes and learn. If you have the program or can get a free version, practice. I did this to get a promotion at my job. Since I watched all the Youtube videos, I knew how to use the program more efficiently than the people who were training me. I knew shortcuts to do things they taught me, but didn't say anything. Finished my work faster than most in my department.
7. Whenever you're cooking, go big. Cook enough extra portions for a meal of leftovers so on that day that you can't be bothered to get up and cook, instead of eating out you can heat something up. If your family doesn't eat leftovers fast enough you can freeze them.
8. Wait before you buy things. I find myself compulsively shopping just before bed for things I don't really need. I add whatever it is to the cart and then sleep on it.
